intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail connecting Marinha to Benagil and take a refreshing swim in the sheltered coves below.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Lagoa, sampling regional red, white, and rosé wines made from indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Arinto. Includes guided cellar tours and paired local cheese and charcuterie tastings.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided tour takes you through hidden grottos and sea arches along the dramatic coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's geological wonders.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Beach Day
experiences.description: Take a traditional boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park with barrier islands, tidal flats, and wildlife. Stop at the pristine Ilha Deserta or Ilha de Tavira for a secluded beach experience far from the crowds, with optional fresh seafood lunch at a local beach shack.

experiences.name: Silves Medieval Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the beautifully preserved Moorish castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, then wander the cobblestone streets of the old town sampling local specialties including cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), medronho brandy, and traditional almond sweets at family-run tascos and markets.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the affordable Aerobus or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your room. Take a short stroll along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings and breathe in the sea air.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby convenience store or a 24-hour café near the resort. Look for a pastel de nata (custard tart) and a light sandwich to keep costs low — budget around €5-8.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. No activities scheduled before landing. Pre-book your airport transfer to save money — shared shuttles cost around €10-15 per person versus €40+ for a private taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and take your first walk along the local beach. September is still warm in the Algarve (avg. 24-27°C) with fewer crowds than summer. Explore the shoreline, find a quiet spot, and enjoy the golden cliffs and turquoise water. Pack a light snack from a nearby bakery to eat on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the local market or town center for a self-guided walking tour. Pick up fresh local fruit, olives, and bread from a mercado (market) for a budget-friendly picnic lunch. Explore the streets, admire the traditional azulejo tile facades, and visit the local church — most are free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade at sunset. Find a local tasca (tavern) for a budget dinner — look for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day), which typically costs €7-10 and includes bread, olives, a main, and sometimes a drink.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local pastelaria (pastry shop) for a galão (milky coffee) and pastel de nata — budget €2-3.
meals.lunch: Self-assembled picnic from the local market: fresh fruit, cheese, bread, and olives — budget €5-7.
meals.dinner: Local tasca with prato do dia — grilled fish or pork with potatoes and salad — budget €8-12 including a glass of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: September is shoulder season in the Algarve — great weather, fewer crowds, and slightly lower prices than July/August. Always ask for the 'menu do dia' at restaurants for the best value.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a bicycle to explore Praia da Marinha or another nearby hidden beach. The Algarve coastline is dotted with spectacular sea caves, rock arches, and grottos. Walk the clifftop trails (free) for stunning panoramic views — the Golden Triangle coastal path is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the sea caves and grottos by renting a kayak or joining a budget group boat tour from the beach. Group tours typically cost €15-20 per person and last 1.5-2 hours. Alternatively, swim and snorkel in the clear September waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and visit a local wine bar or cervejaria (beer hall) for a relaxed evening. Try a glass of Algarve Vinho Regional wine — the region produces excellent, affordable whites and reds.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort if included, or a local café — toast with butter and jam plus coffee for €3-4.
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar: prego no pão (steak sandwich) or bifanas (pork sandwich) — budget €4-6.
meals.dinner: Cervejaria dinner: grilled sardines or lulas grelhadas (grilled squid) with bread and salad — budget €10-14.

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals are typically €10-15/hour. Group boat tours are much cheaper than private — always compare prices at the beach kiosks. Bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local bus to Lagos, one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns (approximately 30-60 minutes depending on your base location, bus fare €3-5). Walk the old town walls, visit the Slave Market Museum (€3 entry), and explore the historic center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — a spectacular series of sea stacks, arches, and grottos just outside Lagos. The clifftop walk is completely free and offers some of the most iconic views in the Algarve. Descend the steps to the water's edge for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Lagos before catching the bus back. The town has many budget-friendly restaurants along Rua 25 de Abril. Try cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) or grilled fish at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Local café in your base town — coffee and toast or a croissant — budget €2-4.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the cliffs at Ponta da Piedade with supplies from a Lagos supermarket — budget €5-7.
meals.dinner: Lagos restaurant: grilled sea bass or cataplana — budget €12-15 including a glass of wine.

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is a must-visit in the Algarve. The Ponta da Piedade walk is best done in the afternoon light. Check local bus schedules in advance — Rede Expressos and Eva Transportes serve most Algarve towns.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at a quieter, less-visited local beach near the resort. September means calmer seas and fewer tourists. Bring a book, snorkel gear, or just relax and enjoy the warm Atlantic waters. Look for hidden cove beaches accessible by short clifftop trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wine cooperative or quinta (wine estate) for an affordable wine tasting. The Algarve produces Denominação de Origem Controlada (DOC) wines — look for Lagoa or Lagos wine cooperatives which offer tastings for €5-10. Many cooperatives also sell bottles at cellar-door prices (€4-8/bottle).
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple dinner using local ingredients purchased from a supermarket or market — fresh Algarve fish, vegetables, and local wine. Most budget accommodations have shared kitchen facilities, which can dramatically cut food costs.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, fresh fruit, and coffee from a local supermarket — budget €3-4.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar: toasted sandwich (tosta mista) and a cold beer — budget €5-7.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner with fresh fish from the market, salad, bread, and a bottle of local wine — budget €10-12 for everything.

day_by_day.notes: Wine cooperative tastings are one of the best budget experiences in the Algarve. Call ahead or check opening hours as some cooperatives close on weekends. The Lagoa Wine Cooperative is particularly well-regarded.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Silves, the former Moorish capital of the Algarve. Catch a local bus or train (Silves has a train station on the Algarve line — tickets from €2-4). Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (€3 entry) with panoramic views over orange groves and the countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves town center — walk along the old city walls, visit the Gothic Cathedral (free), and browse the local shops and artisan stores. Stop at a local café for a bica (espresso) and a slice of almond tart — the Algarve is famous for its almond and fig sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves before heading back — the town has excellent, authentic, non-touristy restaurants. Try arroz de peixe (fish rice) or espetada (meat skewers) at a local tasca.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the resort — coffee and pastry — budget €2-3.
meals.lunch: Silves café lunch: soup, bread, and a main for the menu do dia — budget €8-10.
meals.dinner: Silves tasca dinner: arroz de peixe or grilled pork with local wine — budget €10-13.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is inland and slightly cooler than the coast — perfect for a day away from the beach. The castle is one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. The train from Faro to Silves is scenic and very affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the beach near the resort. Take a long morning swim, practice yoga on the beach, or simply enjoy the September sunshine. Collect seashells, explore rock pools, or walk to a nearby viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bike (€10-15/day from local shops) and cycle along the coastal bike paths. Many Algarve towns have dedicated cycling routes connecting beaches and villages. Stop at a miradouro (viewpoint) for photos and a rest.
day_by_day.evening: Happy hour at a beachfront bar — many Algarve bars offer 2-for-1 cocktails or cheap beer between 5-7pm. Watch the sunset over the Atlantic with a cold Super Bock beer or a glass of local vinho verde.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at a local café: eggs, chouriço, toast, orange juice, and coffee — budget €5-7.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar: piri-piri chicken wrap or fresh grilled fish — budget €6-8.
meals.dinner: Local restaurant: frango no churrasco (charcoal chicken) with fries and salad — one of the best budget meals in Portugal — budget €8-10.

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day — keep it relaxed and low-cost. Cycling is a great free/low-cost way to explore the coastline. Check with the resort or local tourist office for recommended cycling routes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Take a local bus (Eva Transportes, €5-8 each way) or join a budget group tour. Visit the dramatic Sagres Fortress (€3 entry) perched on the Atlantic cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse (free to visit the exterior) — the views are extraordinary. Watch surfers tackle the powerful Atlantic swells at Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta. The area has a wild, end-of-the-world atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres town before the return bus — the village has several affordable fish restaurants. Try percebes (barnacles) or ameijoas à bulhão pato (clams in garlic and coriander) as a starter.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a local café before catching the bus — budget €3-4.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or Sagres snack bar: fresh fish sandwich and water — budget €5-7.
meals.dinner: Sagres seafood restaurant: grilled fish of the day with salad and potatoes — budget €12-15.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente are about 1-1.5 hours from most Algarve base towns. The wind can be strong at the cape even in September — bring a light layer. This is a highlight of any Algarve trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local quinta (wine estate) for a morning wine tasting and vineyard tour. The Algarve has several small, family-run quintas that offer intimate tours for €10-15 per person including tastings. Look for Quinta dos Vales or similar estates near your base.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine tasting, visit a local beach for a relaxing afternoon swim. Many Algarve beaches have natural freshwater showers (free) and basic facilities. Bring a picnic assembled from local market produce.
day_by_day.evening: Wine and cheese evening — purchase a selection of local wines, queijo (cheese), presunto (cured ham), and olives from a supermarket or deli. Enjoy on the beach at sunset or on your resort terrace for a fraction of restaurant prices.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the vineyard tour — yogurt and fruit from the supermarket — budget €3.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market produce: cheese, bread, charcuterie, and fruit — budget €7-9.
meals.dinner: DIY wine and tapas evening: local wine bottle (€4-6), cheese, ham, olives, and bread from supermarket — budget €12-15 total for a generous spread.

day_by_day.notes: Wine tasting day! Call ahead to book vineyard tours as many small quintas require reservations. September is harvest season in the Algarve — you may be able to see or participate in grape harvesting activities.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Faro, the Algarve's capital city. Catch a local bus or train (€3-5 from most Algarve towns). Visit the historic walled Cidade Velha (Old Town) — walk through the Arco da Vila, explore the Cathedral (€3.50 to climb the tower for panoramic views), and wander the cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a stunning lagoon system on Faro's doorstep. Take a budget ferry to Ilha Deserta or Ilha de Faro (€2-5 return) for a pristine, uncrowded beach experience. The lagoon is a UNESCO-recognized ecosystem with flamingos and other wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro's historic center before returning. The old town has several excellent, affordable restaurants. Try bacalhau à brás (shredded codfish with eggs and potatoes) — Portugal's most iconic dish.

meals.breakfast: Faro café near the train/bus station — galão and pastel de nata — budget €2-3.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha Deserta or a snack bar on the island — budget €5-8.
meals.dinner: Faro old town restaurant: bacalhau à brás or seafood rice with house wine — budget €11-14.

day_by_day.notes: Faro is often overlooked by tourists but has a genuinely charming historic center. The Ria Formosa lagoon is one of Portugal's most important natural areas — don't miss it. Ferry schedules vary so check times in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a leisurely morning exploring the area immediately around the Aegean Bliss Resort. Take photos of the beachfront, chat with locals, and visit any spots you may have missed earlier in the trip. Visit a local fish market early in the morning to see the day's catch being sold.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a water sport activity — September is ideal for stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) with calmer seas than summer. Many beach operators offer SUP rentals for €10-15/hour or beginner lessons for €20-25. Alternatively, try bodyboarding with a rented board (€5-8/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate being near the end of your trip. Look for a restaurant with a sea view and try a traditional cataplana (copper pot seafood stew for two) — a true Algarve specialty. Split the cost with a travel companion to keep it budget-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at a local café — coffee, fresh orange juice, eggs, and toast — budget €5-6.
meals.lunch: Fish market find: fresh grilled sardines at a beachside grill — budget €6-8.
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated dinner: cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) shared between two, with wine — budget €18-22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The cataplana is a special splurge worth having at least once in the Algarve. Look for restaurants that prepare it fresh to order — it typically takes 20-30 minutes. Avoid tourist trap restaurants near main squares and look for places with local clientele.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax and soak up the last of the Algarve sunshine. Take final photos of the dramatic cliffs and golden sands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit local souvenir shops and artisan stores for budget-friendly gifts: hand-painted tiles (azulejos), locally produced almond sweets, a bottle of local wine or medronho (arbutus berry brandy), or dried fig confections. Markets and cooperative shops offer the best prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant discovered during the trip. Order a final glass of Algarve wine, reflect on the journey, and enjoy a slow, relaxed Portuguese dinner. Try a sobremesa (dessert) — tarte de amêndoa (almond tart) is a regional specialty.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a beachside café — coffee, fresh fruit, and a pastry — budget €4-5.
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch: fresh salad, grilled fish, and a cold drink — budget €8-10.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a favourite local restaurant: grilled fish or meat, salad, bread, dessert, and wine — budget €15-18.

day_by_day.notes: Last full day — make the most of it! Buy medronho (local brandy) or moscatel wine as affordable, authentic Portuguese gifts. Pack carefully tonight to be ready for tomorrow's departure. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims if applicable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk on the beach — a magical, free experience. Pack your bags, check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort, and store luggage if needed. Enjoy a final pastel de nata and bica at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit any last spots on your list or simply relax near the resort. Head to Faro Airport with plenty of time — allow at least 2 hours before your flight. Take the Aerobus or a shared shuttle from your area (€10-15).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, stunning cliffs, fresh seafood, and authentic Portuguese culture — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final pastelaria visit: bica and pastel de nata — budget €2-3.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the resort or at the airport — budget €8-10.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal — budget €10-15 or bring snacks from a supermarket.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — arrange late checkout or luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Faro Airport is small and manageable. Arrive at least 2 hours before departure. Budget summary: with careful planning, this 13-day Algarve trip can be done for approximately €60-80/day including accommodation, food, transport, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail connecting Marinha to Benagil and take a refreshing swim in the sheltered coves below.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and unwind at the hotel bar with a welcome drink. Light snack from the resort's late-night menu before bed.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the Aegean Bliss Resort bar or room service

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer with the hotel. Keep luggage light for carry-on to speed up arrival. Exchange some euros at the airport if needed. Rest is priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start — enjoy a full buffet breakfast at the resort overlooking the beachfront. After breakfast, take a leisurely stroll along the resort's beach to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the Atlantic and soak in the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Praia dos Três Irmãos or the resort's private beach section for an afternoon of swimming and relaxing. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella. Explore the golden cliffs and sea caves by renting a kayak or paddleboard from the beach concession (~€15–€20/hr).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a local seafood restaurant near the resort — try Restaurante O Zé in Alvor for fresh grilled fish and local Algarve wines. Stroll the Alvor waterfront boardwalk after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort (included or ~€15)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — prego sandwich, fresh fruit, and local beer (~€12–€15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Zé, Alvor — grilled sea bass, local wine (~€25–€35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is ideal — warm (24–28°C) with low humidity. Apply sunscreen generously. This is a recovery/orientation day after your late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or taxi (~20 min) to the iconic Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim. Begin the coastal trail from the clifftop viewpoint, admiring the dramatic golden limestone arches, sea stacks, and turquoise coves. The walk takes about 1.5–2 hours at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach via the wooden staircase for a swim in crystal-clear waters — one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. Snorkeling is excellent here. Pack a picnic or grab lunch at the small beach kiosk. Spend the afternoon sunbathing on the secluded pebble-and-sand cove.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a shower and rest. Evening dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro area) — a Michelin-starred spot offering a tasting menu with regional Algarvian ingredients. Book well in advance.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast at a local pastelaria — galão coffee, pastel de nata, toast (~€6–€8)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic or beach kiosk — sandwiches, local cheese, fruit (~€10–€15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro — tasting menu (~€80–€100 per person, splurge evening)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is a highlight of the trip — wear sturdy shoes for the coastal walk. Arrive early to secure a spot on the beach. Limited parking available; consider arriving by 9:30 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the charming fishing village of Ferragudo. Walk the cobblestone streets, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade overlooking the Arade River estuary, and browse the local fish market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic boat trip from Portimão marina along the Arade River and Algarve coast (~€25–€35 per person, 2 hours). See sea caves, grottos, and dramatic cliff formations from the water. Return to the resort mid-afternoon for a pool session.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening at a local wine bar in Portimão. Try Algarve DOC wines — particularly whites from Arinto and Siria grapes and reds from Negra Mole. Pair with local charcuterie and cheese. Try Bar do Rio or a curated wine shop with tasting flights.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or café near Ferragudo (~€8–€10)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso, Ferragudo — traditional cataplana (seafood stew) for two (~€30–€40 per person)
meals.dinner: Wine bar tasting + charcuterie board in Portimão (~€20–€30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most authentic, less-touristy villages in the Algarve. The cataplana is a must-try regional dish — order 24 hours in advance at some restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), walk the ramparts, and explore the Gothic Cathedral of Silves. Silves is also the heart of Algarve's citrus and wine country.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local winery or quinta near Silves for a guided tour and tasting. Quinta dos Vales or Quinta do Francês offer excellent mid-range wine experiences with Algarve varietals (~€15–€25 per person including tasting). Stroll through the orange groves and vineyards.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves old town — Café Inglês near the castle walls is a beloved local institution with a garden terrace. Try the wild boar stew or fresh fish with local wine.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic in the castle gardens with local bread, olives, cheese, and charcuterie from Silves market (~€10–€15)
meals.dinner: Café Inglês, Silves — main + wine (~€25–€35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is about 30 min drive from most Algarve beach resorts. Consider renting a car for this day for flexibility. The winery visit is a highlight for wine enthusiasts — book ahead on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at Meia Praia — a long, sweeping sandy beach near Lagos, ideal for a long walk, swimming, and watersports. Rent a surfboard or try stand-up paddleboarding (~€20/hr). The beach is wide enough to feel uncrowded even in September.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Lagos old town after lunch. Explore the historic city walls, Igreja de Santo António (beautiful azulejo tiles, free entry), and the Slave Market Museum — one of the most historically significant sites in Portugal. Wander the charming lanes and browse independent shops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar near Ponta da Piedade. Watch the golden hour light illuminate the famous sea stacks and arches. Dinner at A Forja restaurant in Lagos for traditional Algarvian home cooking.

meals.breakfast: Beach café at Meia Praia — scrambled eggs, toast, fresh OJ (~€10–€12)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Meia Praia or packed lunch (~€10–€15)
meals.dinner: A Forja, Lagos — bacalhau, local wine (~€20–€30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is one of the Algarve's most vibrant towns — lively but still authentic. Sunday can be busy; arrive at Meia Praia early. Ponta da Piedade is a short drive or 30-min walk from Lagos centre.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and resort day. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and spend the morning at the resort pool or private beach. Read, journal, or simply do nothing — this is a balance day built into the itinerary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: resort spa treatment (massage or body wrap, ~€60–€80). Or take a gentle yoga or pilates class if offered by the resort. Alternatively, explore the local area on foot or by bike — rent bikes from the resort or a nearby shop (~€15/day).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the resort's main restaurant for convenience. Enjoy a bottle of Algarve or Alentejo wine with your meal and watch the sunset over the Atlantic from the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — take your time
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar — salads, wraps, fresh juice (~€15–€20)
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — 2-course dinner with wine (~€35–€50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are essential on a 13-day trip. Don't over-schedule — the Algarve is best enjoyed slowly. This is also a good day to do laundry, plan the second week, or book remaining restaurant reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic lighthouse and fortress perched on 75m cliffs above the Atlantic. A deeply atmospheric and historic spot. Walk the clifftop paths and watch for migratory birds (September is peak migration season).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — the fortress where Prince Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Exploration. Swim at Praia do Beliche or Praia do Tonel — wild, uncrowded Atlantic beaches with powerful surf.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at O Telheiro do Infante in Sagres — a beloved seafood restaurant with ocean views. Try the grilled barnacles (percebes) and local white wine. Drive back to resort (about 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at a Sagres café on arrival (~€5–€8)
meals.lunch: A Sagres, Sagres town — simple fish lunch with local beer (~€15–€20 per person)
meals.dinner: O Telheiro do Infante — seafood feast (~€30–€40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is about 1–1.5 hours west of the central Algarve. Start early to make the most of the day. The wind at Cabo de São Vicente can be strong even in September — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Ria Formosa Natural Park near Faro — a stunning coastal lagoon system. Join a guided boat tour from Faro marina through the barrier islands, salt marshes, and tidal channels (~€25–€35 per person, 2 hours). Spot flamingos, herons, and other migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) — a pristine, car-free barrier island accessible by ferry. Spend the afternoon on one of the most unspoiled beaches in the Algarve. Crystal-clear shallow lagoon water, perfect for swimming. Return ferry to Faro by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Faro's charming Cidade Velha (Old Town) — walk through the Roman arch gateway, visit the Gothic cathedral (climb the tower for views), and stroll the marina. Dinner at Tasca do Ricky — a local favourite for petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and natural wines.

meals.breakfast: Café Aliança, Faro — historic café, coffee and pastries (~€7–€10)
meals.lunch: Restaurant on Ilha Deserta — fresh fish and salad (~€25–€35 per person)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Ricky, Faro — petiscos and natural wine (~€20–€30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Faro is about 45 min east of the central Algarve. Ferries to Ilha Deserta run from Faro marina — check schedules and book in advance in September. Bring reef shoes for the sandbar areas.

day_by_day.morning: Wine-focused day: Drive north to the Alentejo wine region border area or visit a prominent Algarve winery. Herdade dos Grous or Quinta da Penina offer excellent guided tours and tastings. Learn about the unique terroir of southern Portugal and taste Alentejo's famous Aragonez and Antão Vaz wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine theme with a visit to a local olive oil producer — many Algarve estates combine wine and olive oil production. Taste premium Algarve extra-virgin olive oils alongside local cheeses and honey. Purchase bottles to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Dinner at Vila Vita Parc's Ocean Restaurant in Porches (if budget allows for a splurge) or Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo for a more mid-range option. Pair dinner with a bottle selected from your winery visit.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Winery restaurant or picnic on the estate grounds with wine and local products (~€20–€30 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste, Ferragudo — fresh seafood and Algarve wine (~€30–€40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book winery tours in advance — many require reservations. Designate a driver or arrange a private transfer for the wine day. Some wineries offer transport from Algarve resorts as part of tour packages.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the weekly local market in Portimão or Lagoa (check local market schedules for Friday). Browse stalls of fresh produce, local honey, almonds, figs, carob products, handmade ceramics, and embroidered linens. Stock up on edible souvenirs and picnic supplies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Praia de Carvoeiro — a picturesque small beach framed by ochre cliffs and colourful fishing boats. Swim, snorkel, or join a sea cave kayaking tour from the beach (~€25–€35 per person). Walk the Algar Seco clifftop boardwalk for dramatic rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a clifftop bar in Carvoeiro. Dinner at Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro village — a charming, intimate restaurant with excellent fresh fish and a good Portuguese wine list.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh bread, local cheese, fruit, coffee (~€8–€12)
meals.lunch: Beachside café in Carvoeiro — grilled sardines, salad, local beer (~€15–€20)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca, Carvoeiro — 2 courses + wine (~€25–€35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Carvoeiro is one of the most photogenic villages in the Algarve. The Algar Seco walk is short (30 min) but spectacular. Friday evening brings a lively atmosphere to Carvoeiro's village square.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favourite beach from the trip or explore Praia da Rocha near Portimão, a wide golden beach backed by dramatic cliffs and a lively promenade. Enjoy a final long swim in the Atlantic and soak up the September sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Treat yourself to a final spa session at the resort or a hammam experience in Portimão (~€40–€60). Pack non-essentials and begin organizing luggage. Take a final walk along the beachfront at golden hour.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — book a table at a top local restaurant. Restaurante Largo do Paço in Tavira (if willing to drive) or Vilalara Thalassa Resort's restaurant for an elevated beachfront dining experience. Toast to the trip with a bottle of Algarve sparkling wine (espumante).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — enjoy the views one last time
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — grilled fish, salad, rosé wine (~€20–€25)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top local restaurant — 3 courses + wine (~€50–€70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy any remaining souvenirs today — local ceramics, Flor de Sal sea salt, Algarve almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), and wine make excellent gifts. Confirm checkout time and airport transfer for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the beach. Enjoy a final breakfast at the resort. Check out and store luggage with the concierge if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: visit a nearby craft shop or wine store for last-minute purchases. Or relax at a café in the nearest town with a galão and pastel de nata, reflecting on the trip. Transfer to Faro Airport (~45 min from most Algarve resorts).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Arrive at least 2 hours before your flight. Pick up duty-free Portuguese wine, ginjinha, or local products at the airport shops.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or café stop
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café before airport transfer (~€10–€15) or airport restaurant
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer the night before. Faro Airport is small but can get busy on Sunday mornings — allow extra time. Portuguese customs allows wine purchases within EU duty-free limits. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Walk the clifftop trail connecting Marinha to Benagil and take a refreshing swim in the sheltered coves below.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Lagoa, sampling regional red, white, and rosé wines made from indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Arinto. Includes guided cellar tours and paired local cheese and charcuterie tastings.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided tour takes you through hidden grottos and sea arches along the dramatic coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's geological wonders.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Beach Day
experiences.description: Take a traditional boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park with barrier islands, tidal flats, and wildlife. Stop at the pristine Ilha Deserta or Ilha de Tavira for a secluded beach experience far from the crowds, with optional fresh seafood lunch at a local beach shack.

experiences.name: Silves Medieval Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the beautifully preserved Moorish castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, then wander the cobblestone streets of the old town sampling local specialties including cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), medronho brandy, and traditional almond sweets at family-run tascos and markets.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) will whisk you directly to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled Champagne and a light fruit & cheese platter prepared by the resort — and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.dinner: Light welcome platter in-suite upon arrival, courtesy of the resort

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request late check-in amenities when booking. Keep the first night relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely full breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Take a slow morning stroll along the private beach, acclimating to the warm Algarve air and turquoise waters. Arrange for a beach cabana setup with chilled towels and refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk & Swim — one of the Algarve's crown jewels. Explore dramatic golden limestone cliffs, hidden grottos, and crystalline coves. Swim in the sheltered emerald waters. A private guide can be arranged for an exclusive, unhurried experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail at the infinity pool bar. Dress for dinner and head to a top-tier local restaurant such as Ocean Restaurant (Vila Vita Parc) or Henrique Leis for an innovative tasting menu showcasing modern Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort, enjoyed on the rocks at Praia da Marinha with chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc or Henrique Leis — Michelin-starred tasting menu with wine pairing (reserve in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is approximately 10–15 minutes from most Algarve coastal resorts. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the coastal path. Book dinner reservations well in advance for Michelin-starred venues.

day_by_day.morning: Private Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — depart by luxury vehicle to Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Lagoa. Begin with an exclusive behind-the-scenes winery tour, learning about Algarve's unique terroir, indigenous grape varieties (Negra Mole, Castelão), and winemaking philosophy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with a guided tasting of premium reserve wines, late-harvest dessert wines, and local spirits such as medronho (arbutus brandy). Pair tastings with artisanal local cheeses, charcuterie, and freshly baked bread at the vineyard's estate.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing sunset swim. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, requesting a sommelier-curated wine pairing menu to complement the day's wine discoveries.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast with fresh pastries, yogurt, seasonal fruits, and espresso
meals.lunch: Vineyard estate lunch — artisanal charcuterie, local cheeses, olives, and bread paired with estate wines in a rustic quinta setting
meals.dinner: Resort's signature restaurant — premium seafood tasting menu with Algarve wine pairing selected by the in-house sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transport for the wine tour to ensure a safe, comfortable return. Quinta dos Vales is approximately 30–40 minutes from the coastal resort area. Purchase a few bottles of your favorites to enjoy throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — embark on an exclusive private kayak excursion to the world-famous Benagil Cave. Paddle through sea arches, hidden grottoes, and golden cliffs at your own pace with a private guide. Enter the cathedral-like interior of the cave and swim in its magical domed chamber.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on the secluded beach near Benagil. Alternatively, arrange a private boat charter to explore additional hidden sea caves and secret beaches along the Algarve coastline that are inaccessible by foot.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the resort terrace with local sparkling wine and petiscos (Portuguese tapas). Dinner at a premium local seafood restaurant such as Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo or A Tasca in Portimão — fresh catch of the day in an intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast featuring fresh-baked bread, regional honey, local jams, smoked fish, and a full egg station
meals.lunch: Light seaside lunch at a beach restaurant near Benagil — grilled fish, salads, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo) or A Tasca (Portimão) — whole grilled sea bass, cataplana seafood stew, and local white wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the private kayak tour in advance, especially in September when demand remains high. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring a waterproof bag for valuables. The Benagil Cave is best visited in the morning before afternoon winds pick up.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a full resort spa morning — book a signature Portuguese stone massage or a seaweed body wrap using locally sourced Atlantic ingredients. Follow with time in the hammam, sauna, and hydrotherapy pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private beach afternoon at the resort — arrange a luxury cabana with personalized service, chilled rosé, fresh fruit platters, and a dedicated beach butler. Take a stand-up paddleboard or kayak out on the calm September waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the Algarve coast — watch the golden cliffs glow at dusk while sipping Champagne on deck. Return for a late dinner at the resort or a nearby fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in-suite with panoramic sea views — smoked salmon, avocado toast, pastéis de nata, and fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled octopus salad, gazpacho, and sparkling water with citrus
meals.dinner: Sunset catamaran dinner cruise with a curated menu of petiscos and chilled wines, or resort fine dining upon return

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa well in advance — Saturday slots fill quickly. The sunset catamaran cruise typically departs around 17:30–18:00 in September. Bring a light layer for the boat as sea breezes can be cool after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Medieval Castle & Old Town Food Walk — depart by private car to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificently preserved red sandstone castle with panoramic views over the orange groves and hills. Visit the Gothic cathedral and the Roman bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a private food walk through Silves' charming old town — taste local specialties including carob products, fig and almond sweets, smoked sausages, and traditional Algarvian pastries. Visit the local market (if open) and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via a scenic drive through the Algarve countryside. Enjoy a quiet evening with a private in-suite dinner arranged by the resort chef — a curated menu of Algarvian classics with premium wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Portuguese spread with fresh bread, cold cuts, local cheeses, and strong espresso
meals.lunch: Traditional tasca lunch in Silves — ameijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams), grilled chicken piri-piri, and house red wine in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's dinner at the resort — slow-roasted lamb, cataplana de marisco, and a curated Algarve wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 30–45 minutes inland from the coast. September temperatures inland can be warmer than the coast, so bring light, breathable clothing and sun protection. The castle is open daily and rarely crowded on weekday mornings.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Beach Day — depart by private transfer to Faro. Board a premium private boat for an exclusive tour of the Ria Formosa lagoon system. Glide through tranquil channels, spot flamingos, herons, and migratory birds, and explore the unique barrier island ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dock at one of the pristine barrier island beaches (Ilha Deserta or Ilha da Culatra) — among the most unspoiled beaches in Portugal. Swim in crystal-clear, shallow lagoon waters, sunbathe on white sand, and enjoy a private seafood lunch prepared on board or at a local beachside restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro by boat and transfer back to the resort. Evening at leisure — enjoy a cocktail at the resort bar and a relaxed dinner at a nearby premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — yogurt parfait, granola, fresh fruit, and espresso to fuel the day
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on Ilha Deserta — grilled fish, percebes (barnacles), local oysters, and chilled Alvarinho wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos (Faro) or resort dining — duck rice, salt cod with chickpeas, and regional dessert wines

day_by_day.notes: Ria Formosa is approximately 45–60 minutes from the western Algarve. Book a private boat charter for the most exclusive experience. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and binoculars for birdwatching. September is an excellent time for migratory bird sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia da Marinha for an early-morning swim and photography walk along the cliffs — September light in the morning is golden and spectacular. Explore sections of the coastal trail not covered on Day 2, discovering hidden arches and sea stacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht charter afternoon — sail along the Algarve coast, anchoring at secluded coves for swimming and snorkeling. Enjoy chilled Champagne, fresh fruit, and canapés on deck with personalized crew service.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the resort's infinity pool with a signature cocktail. Dinner at a premium local restaurant — Vila Joya (two Michelin stars, Albufeira) for an extraordinary fine-dining experience with an Austrian-Portuguese fusion tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Light in-suite breakfast — fresh fruit, Greek yogurt, and espresso before the early coastal walk
meals.lunch: On-board yacht lunch — charcuterie boards, fresh sushi-grade fish ceviche, local cheeses, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Vila Joya (Albufeira) — two Michelin-star tasting menu with exceptional wine pairing (must book weeks in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Vila Joya is one of Portugal's most celebrated fine-dining destinations and requires advance reservation. The private yacht charter can be arranged through the resort's concierge. Bring a light jacket for the evening boat return.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private wine masterclass at the resort or a nearby quinta — a sommelier leads an in-depth session on Algarve and Alentejo wines, covering viticulture, tasting techniques, and food pairing. A perfect complement to the vineyard visit on Day 3.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming coastal town of Lagos — stroll through the historic old town, visit the Igreja de Santo António, and browse the vibrant local market. Walk to Ponta da Piedade for breathtaking views of the most dramatic rock formations in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a cliffside bar in Lagos. Dinner at Casinha do Petisco or Adega da Marina in Lagos — fresh local seafood, traditional cataplana, and excellent regional wines in a warm, authentic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Resort champagne brunch — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon blinis, pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Casual premium lunch in Lagos — grilled sea bream, tomato salad, and local craft beer or sparkling water
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco or Adega da Marina, Lagos — cataplana de marisco, grilled percebes, and local Algarve red wine

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 20–40 minutes from the central Algarve resort area. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the late afternoon for golden-hour light. The old town of Lagos is largely pedestrianized and easily walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury spa morning — book a couples' or solo full-body ritual including a hot stone massage, facial, and body scrub using local ingredients (Atlantic sea salt, carob, and almond oil). Spend time in the resort's thermal circuit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided jeep safari into the Algarve hinterland — explore cork oak forests, traditional whitewashed villages, and hidden countryside viewpoints. Stop at a local farm to taste freshly pressed olive oil, regional honey, and homemade jams.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a golden-hour swim. Private beachside dinner arranged by the resort — a candlelit table on the sand with a bespoke menu crafted by the executive chef, paired with premium Portuguese wines.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast with fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, and artisanal coffee
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch during the jeep safari — rustic bread, local cheeses, olive oil, honey, and charcuterie in a countryside setting
meals.dinner: Private candlelit beachside dinner at the resort — five-course bespoke menu with sommelier wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The private beachside dinner must be arranged with the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. The jeep safari is a wonderful way to experience the authentic Algarve beyond the coast. Bring a light layer for the evening beach dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tavira — one of the most beautiful and authentic towns in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins, the charming whitewashed streets, and the stunning Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo. Hire a private guide for a curated historical walking tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island with pristine beaches and calm waters. Relax on the wide, uncrowded sands, swim in the warm September sea, and enjoy the tranquility of one of the Algarve's most beautiful islands.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira before returning to the resort — Quatro Águas or Restaurante Páteo da Galé for outstanding fresh seafood in an elegant riverside or garden setting.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread with local specialties, fresh juices, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch on Ilha de Tavira — grilled fish, salads, and chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Quatro Águas or Páteo da Galé, Tavira — fresh clams, grilled turbot, and regional white wines

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 60–75 minutes east of the central Algarve. Arrange private transport for the day. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs frequently in September. Tavira is considered one of the most authentically Portuguese towns in the Algarve — a must-visit.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — a leisurely swim and walk along the resort's private beach. Collect shells, take photographs, and soak in the last full day of Algarve sunshine. Arrange a professional sunrise photography session on the beach if desired.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Algarve Wine & Vineyard experience for a final wine farewell — visit a different producer (e.g., Quinta da Tôr or Monte da Casteleja near Lagos) for a premium reserve tasting and the opportunity to purchase wines to take home. Arrange shipping of selected bottles if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — return to one of the trip's most beloved restaurants or try a new premium venue such as Restaurante Ameijoa (Portimão) or book a private chef dinner at the resort with a fully bespoke menu celebrating the flavors of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Champagne farewell breakfast on the resort terrace — full spread with all favorites from the trip
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the vineyard estate — tapas, charcuterie, and a final glass of Algarve rosé
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — premium tasting menu at a top-tier local restaurant or private resort chef dinner with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange wine shipping or purchase premium wine bags for carry-on if bringing bottles home. Use the afternoon winery visit to stock up on favorite discoveries from the trip. Confirm departure logistics with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a last sunrise walk on the beach, a final dip in the resort pool, and a relaxed farewell breakfast. Pack and prepare for departure, savoring the last moments of the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport. Depart Portugal with unforgettable memories of golden cliffs, world-class wines, and extraordinary cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — in-flight or onward journey

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a full, leisurely spread with all favorites: pastéis de nata, smoked fish, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Light airport lounge lunch or early lunch at the resort before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-out, transfer, and airport procedures. The resort concierge can arrange luggage storage if the flight is later in the day. Request a late check-out (subject to availability) to maximize your final morning.
